raw_arguments.summary: Outbox arrivals (2880 in 900 s, about 3.2/s) exceeded publication throughput (1980, about 2.2/s). The backlog grew from 12 to 912 and the oldest undelivered age from 0.8 s to 410 s. Deliveries all succeeded, so the lateness is queueing delay at the single poller, not failures.

findings.claim: The outbox is accumulating a backlog because publication throughput is lower than the arrival rate.
findings.reason: 2880 arrivals vs 1980 publications in 900 s; pending gauge rose 12 to 912 (a gap of 900) and oldest undelivered age rose 0.8 s to 410 s.

findings.claim: Transfer requests and deliveries are healthy, so the delay is not from request handling or delivery errors.
findings.reason: All 2885 transfers returned 201 with p95 0.24 s and no restarts; all 1980 delivery attempts succeeded; failed count is 0.

findings.claim: Each delivery takes about 450 ms, mostly in the consumer handler (about 401 ms) plus auth (about 51 ms), with almost no unattributed time.
findings.reason: total_ms p50 452 and p95 470; handler_ms p50 401; auth_ms p50 51; unattributed_ms p50 1.2.

findings.claim: The single poller is probably limited by sequential delivery, capping throughput near the observed 2.2/s, below the 3.2/s arrival rate.
findings.reason: One poller with a 1000 ms poll interval and batch size 20, plus about 0.45 s per delivery, is consistent with the observed ~2.2/s ceiling. The poller loop itself was not observed.

alternatives.hypothesis: The consumer handler is slow (about 400 ms) and is the real bottleneck rather than the poller configuration.
alternatives.reason: Handler time dominates each attempt, but the consumer here is a fixture, so its latency may not match production.

alternatives.hypothesis: Delivery failures or retries are causing the delay.
alternatives.reason: Failed count is 0 and all 1980 delivery records are SUCCESS with no network or server errors.

alternatives.hypothesis: Slow transfer request handling is delaying the notifications.
alternatives.reason: Transfer p95 is 0.24 s, all responses are 201, and there were no restarts.

limitations: Only the 15-minute window was observed, so the onset and any earlier baseline are unknown.
The consumer is a fixture, so production handler latency may differ.
The poller's loop behavior (sequential vs concurrent, how a batch is drained) was not observed directly.
No customer-side notification timestamps were observed, only outbox-side age.
next_checks: Inspect the poller loop to see whether a batch of 20 is delivered sequentially and what the effective cycle time is.
Test a larger batch size, a shorter poll interval, or several pollers or concurrent delivery in a non-production environment and watch the backlog.
Measure real consumer handler latency in production to see if about 400 ms is representative.
Check the pending gauge and oldest-age history before 12:00Z to find when the backlog started growing.

raw_arguments.summary: The outbox publisher is throughput-limited, so it falls behind committed transfers. Arrivals were 2880 against 1980 publications in 900 s, and the backlog grew from 12 to 912 with the oldest undelivered age reaching 410 s. Deliveries that do run succeed and are fast. The cause of the limit is inferred from config, not directly observed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Poll interval (1000 ms) or batch size (20) is the binding limit rather than serial delivery time.
alternatives.reason: 20 per 1 s poll would allow up to 20/s, well above the observed 2.2/s, so these alone do not explain the rate.

alternatives.hypothesis: The slow consumer handler (about 401 ms) is the main contributor to per-attempt time.

limitations: Serial delivery by the single poller is inferred from config and timing arithmetic, not directly observed.
